title: Semi-Automatic Graphical Tool for Measuring Coronary Artery Spatially Weighted Calcium Score from Gated Cardiac Computed Tomography Images
protocol: Create a main folder for the project in the files directory.
Within the main folder, create two new folders.
Rename the first folder to "Original_Data".
Create a new folder within the "Original_Data" folder for each patient.
Rename each patient folder with an anonymized identifier.
Import complete set of raw DICOM files into each patient folder.
Rename the second folder to "Meta_Data".
Download the program file and cover art image from the specified sources.
Move the downloaded files from the downloads folder to the main project folder by dragging and dropping.
Launch the program by double-clicking its file in the main project folder.
Open the editor window by single-clicking anywhere on it.
Click the green Run button located in the top ribbon of the editor tab to start the program.
After opening, navigate to the Open DICOM button in the bottom left corner.
Open the files directory and navigate to the project's main folder containing original data.
Select a patient's folder for analysis by single-clicking on it.
Click Open to proceed with analyzing the selected patient's data.
Scroll up and down until crosshairs are in the center of the 0 mg/mL phantom.
Single-click to place a 10-by-10 grid of points on the current slice and its neighboring two slices.
Repeat steps for the 100 mg/mL phantom.
Click the No Phantom button if phantoms are unavailable or unusable due to quality issues.
Begin tracing each of the four coronary arteries by clicking one of the artery buttons: LAD, LCA, LCX, or RCA.
Hover over the axial view and scroll to navigate to either the proximal or distal end of the chosen artery.
Observe the shape of the artery in this slice.
If the shape is circular in the axial view and at most 5 mm in diameter, follow these sub-steps.
Place a point on the center of the artery in the axial view.
Delete the point by double-clicking if it does not fit within a 5 mm diameter circle.
Move to the sagittal or coronal view and place a point that aligns with the center of the artery in the axial view.
If necessary, delete an accidentally placed point by rapidly double-clicking on it in any view.
Click on the Draw ROI button if the artery is not circular in the axial plane.
Zoom in or out using the scroll function to trace around the artery in the axial view.
Delete a previously clicked point during tracing using the backspace key while the ROI is open.
Double-click where the last point should be placed to close the ROI.
Refine the closed ROI by dragging its perimeter points or adding new points by double-clicking on its perimeter.
Scroll up or down one slice in the axial view and repeat steps until the end of the chosen artery is reached.
Re-click on the finished artery's button to review the tracing of the artery and ensure no accidental points were placed.
Move on to the next of the four arteries.
Repeat steps 3.6-3.10 for each artery.
Click the SWCS button in the bottom right corner when all four arteries have been traced.
Wait until "Done Processing" is displayed in the bottom left area.
Close the program window by clicking the red button in the top left corner (Mac) or the X button in the top right corner (PC).
Open the files directory and navigate to the project's main folder.
Go into the Meta_Data folder.
Notice a new folder with the same name as the original data folder for that subject.
Review the PDFs within this folder to get the final SWCS and Agatston score for the case, as well as the weighting function used.
